extracted.intended_audience: suppliers of water for community public water systems, laboratories performing UCMR analyses, and State/EPA regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for laboratory validation, quality control, monitoring, reporting, and technology/treatment standards under EPA CFR Part 141 (Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring, MCLGs, MCLs, BATs, and related monitoring provisions). Targeted at water suppliers, testing laboratories, and State/EPA compliance staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Reporting Level (MRL) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The MRL is defined by EPA as the quantitation limit achievable, with 95 percent confidence, by 75 percent of laboratories nationwide, assuming the use of good instrumentation and experienced analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of laboratory performance — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must be capable of quantifying each contaminant listed in Table 1 at or below the MRL specified and must complete and keep on file records of two distinct procedures: an Initial Demonstration of Capability (IDC) involving replicate analyses at or below the MRL and, for each day UCMR analyses are conducted, a validation of ability to quantify each contaminant at or below the MRL following the daily validation procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of both procedures must be available for inspection; the initial validation procedure is described in the regulation and must be followed exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration curve regression model and calibration range
rubrics_metrics.description: The MRL (or any concentration below the MRL being evaluated) must be contained within the range of calibration. Only straight line or quadratic regression models are allowed; weighted or unweighted models may be used; cubic regression models are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The calibration curve regression model and the range of calibration levels used in performance validation steps must be used in all routine sample analyses used to comply with this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicate analyses for IDC
rubrics_metrics.description: Replicate analyses of at least seven (7) fortified samples in reagent water must be performed at or below the MRL for each analyte and processed through the entire method procedure (including extraction and preservatives, where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least seven replicates are required; results are used to calculate the prediction interval and validate laboratory performance at the MRL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction Interval of Results (PIR) calculation and use
rubrics_metrics.description: A Prediction Interval of Results (PIR), based on the estimated arithmetic mean and the estimated sample standard deviation of measurement results, must be determined using the specified equations involving Student's t, sample standard deviation, and number of replicates; the Half Range PIR (HRPIR) is a constant factor (C) times the standard deviation (Table 3 lists C for 7–10 replicates at 99% Student's t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use number of replicates (n), Student's t value for two-sided 99% confidence, mean of replicates, and sample standard deviation; compute HRPIR and PIR using the regulation's equations and Table 3 constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIR percent recovery pass/fail criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The lower and upper result limits of the PIR must be converted to percent recovery of the concentration being tested. To pass at a given level, the PIR lower recovery limit cannot be lower than the QC interval lower limit (50%) and the PIR upper recovery limit cannot be greater than the QC interval upper limit (150%). If either PIR limit falls outside the 50%–150% QC interval, laboratory performance is not validated at the concentration evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PIR limits are within 50%–150%, laboratory performance is validated for that analyte at that concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily performance check requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an IDC demonstrates DQOs are met at or below an MRL, a daily performance check must be performed for each analyte and method: a single laboratory blank fortified at or below the MRL must be processed through the entire method procedure and its measured concentration converted to percent recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily check recovery must be within 50%–150% (inclusive) to validate daily performance. If recovery cannot be demonstrated, results for that analyte are not valid. Laboratories may re-run the daily performance check; if validated, performance is considered validated. Alternatively, the lab may re-calibrate and repeat validation for all analytes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-defined quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must analyze Laboratory Fortified Blanks (LFBs) and conduct Laboratory Performance Checks as appropriate to the method requirements for methods listed in the regulation; each method specifies acceptance criteria for these QC checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow individual method QC acceptance criteria as specified in each analytical method incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use the same calibration model in routine analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The calibration curve regression model and the range of calibration levels used in performance validation steps must be used in future routine sample analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency between validation and routine analysis is mandatory; prohibited to use cubic polynomial models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting timeframe and approval workflow for laboratory data
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must post and approve UCMR data in EPA's electronic data reporting system within 90 days from the sample collection date. The supplier (PWS) then has 30 days from when the laboratory posts and approves data to review, approve, and submit data to the State and EPA via the electronic data reporting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the supplier does not electronically approve and submit within 30 days of the lab posting approved data, the data will be considered approved by the supplier and available for State and EPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation definitions — monitoring and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any failure to monitor in accordance with §141.40(a)(3)-(5) is a monitoring violation. Any failure to report in accordance with §141.35 is a reporting violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governors' petition for additional contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: Governors of seven or more States may petition the EPA Administrator to add contaminants to the UCMR Contaminant List. The petition must clearly identify reasons for adding the contaminant(s), including potential public health risk, information on disproportional risks to children, expected occurrence documented by available data, any analytical methods known or proposed to test for the contaminant(s), and other relevant information to assist the Administrator's determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition content must be specific and provide evidence/data and analytical method information to support adding contaminants.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-wide waivers for unregulated contaminant monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may apply to EPA for a State-wide waiver from unregulated contaminant monitoring for PWSs serving more than 10,000 people by submitting an application that includes the list of contaminants for which a waiver is requested and documentation for each demonstrating that the contaminants or their parent compounds do not occur naturally in the State and certifying no use, application, storage, disposal, release, or detection in source waters or distribution systems during the past 15 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will review and notify the State whether it accepts or rejects the request; the State must receive written EPA approval before issuing a State-wide waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of analytical methods and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified methods and standards (e.g., EPA Method 200.7; Method 537.1; Method 533; Standard Methods SM 3120 B; ASTM D1976-20) are incorporated by reference into the regulation with approval of the Director of the Federal Register and are available for inspection at listed repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratories and systems must use these approved methods where applicable; availability information and contact details are provided in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special monitoring for sodium — sampling frequency and sample point
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppliers of water for community public water systems shall collect and analyze one sample per plant at the entry point of the distribution system for sodium concentration levels: annually for systems utilizing surface water sources in whole or part, and at least every three years for systems utilizing solely ground water sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum number of samples is based on number of treatment plants; multiple wells drawing from a single aquifer may be considered one treatment plant with State approval; States may require more frequent sampling where sodium content is variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special monitoring for sodium — reporting and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplier shall report sodium analysis results to EPA and/or the State within the first 10 days of the month following the month in which the sample results were received or within the first 10 days following the end of the required monitoring period as stipulated by the State, whichever is first. The supplier shall notify appropriate local and State public health officials of sodium levels by written notice by direct mail within three months, and send a copy of each such notice to EPA and/or the State within 10 days of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State has adopted the regulation and reports results, the supplier need not report to EPA; otherwise the supplier must report to EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special monitoring for corrosivity characteristics — distribution system materials identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water supply systems shall identify whether specified construction materials are present in their distribution system and report to the State. Materials to identify include: lead (from piping, solder, caulking, interior lining, alloys, home plumbing), copper (piping, alloys, service lines, home plumbing), galvanized piping, ferrous piping (cast iron and steel), asbestos cement pipe; States may require reporting of other materials (e.g., vinyl-lined asbestos cement pipe, coal tar lined pipes and tanks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum Contaminant Level Goals (MCLGs) for organic contaminants — zero-list and numeric values
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLGs are zero for a specified list of organic contaminants (e.g., Benzene, Vinyl chloride, Carbon tetrachloride, etc., including PFOA and PFOS). Additional organic contaminants have specified numeric MCLGs listed in the regulation (table of contaminants and mg/L values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory citations and amendments are noted; the list includes both zero MCLGs and specific numeric values for other organics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS Hazard Index and HBWCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The PFAS Mixture Hazard Index (HI) is the sum of component hazard quotients (HQs), calculated by dividing the measured component PFAS concentration in water by the contaminant's health-based water concentration (HBWC) expressed in the same units; an HI greater than 1 indicates an exceedance and potential human health risk. HBWCs: PFHxS = 10 ng/l; HFPO-DA = 10 ng/l; PFNA = 10 ng/l; PFBS = 2000 ng/l. Hazard Index formula and units are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation provides the Hazard Index formula and clarifies units (ng/l) and abbreviations (HBWC, HQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLGs for inorganic contaminants — numeric values and effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLGs for specified inorganic contaminants are listed with numeric values (e.g., Arsenic = zero [effective date noted], Barium = 2 mg/L, Lead = zero, Fluoride = 4.0 mg/L, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some values include effective dates or transitional provisions; regulatory history and amendments are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLGs for microbiological contaminants and compliance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLGs for specified microbiological contaminants (Giardia lamblia, Viruses, Legionella, Total coliforms, Cryptosporidium, E. coli) are zero. Until March 31, 2016, the total coliform MCL is based on presence/absence with monthly percentage/sample count compliance thresholds; beginning April 1, 2016, compliance for E. coli is determined under specified conditions. Specific conditions constitute violations (e.g., fecal coliform-positive repeat sample, E. coli-positive repeat sample, failures to take required repeat samples or to test for E. coli on repeat positives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems collecting ≥40 samples/month: no more than 5.0% may be total coliform-positive; for systems collecting <40 samples/month: no more than one total coliform-positive per month. Violation may pose an acute risk to health per public notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technologies and measures identified as BATs or means to achieve microbial and other MCL compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For total coliforms/E. coli, the Administrator identifies protection of wells, maintenance of disinfectant residual, proper distribution system maintenance, filtration/disinfection (per relevant subparts), and compliance with EPA-approved State Wellhead Protection Programs as appropriate technologies/treatment techniques/means available for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are also identified as affordable technologies for systems serving 10,000 or fewer people where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLs and BATs for organic contaminants and PFAS (treatment technology identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation sets numeric MCLs for volatile and synthetic organic contaminants (Table 1 and paragraph (c)) and identifies Best Available Technologies (BATs) for achieving compliance for those contaminants (Table 2 lists GAC, PTA, OX applicability). For PFAS, BATs identified include anion exchange, GAC, reverse osmosis, and nanofiltration. Small System Compliance Technologies (SSCTs) for PFAS include GAC and Anion Exchange for all small system categories and Reverse Osmosis/Nanofiltration for systems serving 3,301–10,000 persons, with notes on affordability and technical feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables list specific contaminants mapped to BATs/SSCTs. Notes indicate limitations (e.g., technologies that reject large volumes of water may not be appropriate where water quantity is an issue).

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLs for inorganic contaminants and BAT mapping (including key to BATs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants are listed (e.g., Fluoride 4.0 mg/L, Arsenic 0.010 mg/L, etc.) and the Administrator identifies BATs for each inorganic contaminant (Table maps chemicals to BAT numeric codes). A key explains numeric BAT codes (1 = Activated Alumina; 2 = Coagulation/Filtration; 3 = Direct and Diatomite Filtration; 4 = Granular Activated Carbon; 5 = Ion Exchange; 6 = Lime Softening; 7 = Reverse Osmosis; 8 = Corrosion Control; 9 = Electrodialysis; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some BATs have limitations (e.g., not BAT for systems <500 service connections; pre-oxidation may be required for certain arsenic species; iron:arsenic ratio guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small System Compliance Technologies (SSCTs) for arsenic
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator identifies affordable technologies/means available to systems serving ≤10,000 persons for achieving arsenic MCL compliance (e.g., Activated Alumina centralized and point-of-use, Coagulation/Filtration, Coagulation-assisted Microfiltration, Electrodialysis reversal, Enhanced coagulation/filtration, Enhanced lime softening, Ion Exchange, Lime Softening, Oxidation/Filtration, Reverse Osmosis centralized and point-of-use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: POU/POE devices used for compliance require programs to ensure proper long-term operation, maintenance, and monitoring; some technologies are unlikely to be installed solely for arsenic removal or may require pH adjustment or reject large water volumes; SSCTs correspond to system size categories per SDWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLs for disinfection byproducts and MRDLGs for disinfectants
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLs for disinfection byproducts are specified (e.g., Bromate 0.010 mg/L, Chlorite 1.0 mg/L) and MRDLGs for disinfectants are set (Chlorine and Chloramines MRDLG 4 mg/L as Cl2; Chlorine dioxide 0.8 mg/L as ClO2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance dates for systems (e.g., Subpart H systems serving 10,000+ persons must comply beginning January 1, 2002) are provided where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLGs for radionuclides
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLGs for radionuclides are listed (Combined radium-226 and -228 = Zero; Gross alpha particle activity excluding radon and uranium = Zero; Beta particle and photon radioactivity = Zero; Uranium = Zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for sections and paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation specifies effective dates for various paragraphs/sections (e.g., effective dates for portions of §141.61 are January 9, 1989; July 30, 1992; January 17, 1994; and April 26, 2029 for certain subparagraphs; §141.62 effective dates similarly specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance and implementation scheduling for different provisions are specified and should be checked for each paragraph referenced.
